title: Maintaining Cross-Platform Libraries
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of maintaining cross-platform libraries using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates maintaining cross-platform libraries.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Maintaining Cross-Platform Libraries** as part of **Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, and Kotlin/Native**. Apply maintaining cross-platform libraries by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—API Design Across Targets, Platform-Specific Edge Cases, Documentation and Compatibility Testing—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Cross-platform targets differ in runtime APIs, toolchains, and support maturity. Check the current compatibility matrix before committing to a production target.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Apply maintaining cross-platform libraries by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with api design across targets. Then compare it with platform-specific edge cases. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: API Design Across Targets
items.text: API Design Across Targets crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

items.title: Platform-Specific Edge Cases
items.text: Platform-Specific Edge Cases is one part of maintaining cross-platform libraries. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Documentation and Compatibility Testing
items.text: Documentation and Compatibility Testing means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run inside a Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, or Kotlin/Native project configured for the selected target. Verify platform support and maturity before production use.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Maintaining Cross-Platform Libraries removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

items.title: Explain
items.text: Describe the main rule of maintaining cross-platform libraries in your own words.

items.title: Apply
items.text: Change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Check one edge case and the official reference for the selected Kotlin/runtime version.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates maintaining cross-platform libraries. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving api design across targets.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain maintaining cross-platform libraries without copying the lesson wording.
Demonstrate the concept with a small code/configuration change and state the expected result.
Test one boundary case or explain a relevant platform/version limitation.
hints: Begin with the first syllabus subtopic: API Design Across Targets. What input or state does it act on?
Change only one value, branch, declaration, or dependency at a time. Predict what should happen before running the code.
Compare your observed result with the expected output and the official reference; verify that you are using the required project type and dependency set.
